docs.summary: Turns a sprite's alpha silhouette into a tight polygon mesh: it traces the opaque region's outline, simplifies it, and triangulates it. The outline paths are returned alongside the mesh so a future 2D physics collider can reuse the exact same geometry. All coordinates are in pixel space with a bottom-left origin (matching [`SpriteRect`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.SpriteRect) / UV space).

members.name: Generate
members.signature: public static TracedMesh Generate(byte[] alpha, int width, int height, byte alphaThreshold = 1, float simplifyTolerance = 1.5f)

docs.summary: Traces + simplifies + triangulates a binary alpha mask. `alpha` is row-major with a bottom-left origin (length `width*height`); a texel counts as opaque when its value is >= `alphaThreshold`. `simplifyTolerance` is the maximum deviation (in pixels) allowed when collapsing the staircase outline into straight edges; higher = fewer vertices.

members.name: TraceContours
members.signature: public static List<Float2[]> TraceContours(byte[] alpha, int width, int height, byte alphaThreshold = 1)

docs.summary: Extracts the opaque region's boundary as closed loops of grid-corner points. Each unit boundary between an opaque and a transparent (or out-of-bounds) cell becomes an oriented edge with the opaque side on its left; the edges are then stitched into loops. Outer loops wind counter-clockwise.

members.name: Simplify
members.signature: public static Float2[] Simplify(Float2[] points, float tolerance)

docs.summary: Douglas-Peucker simplification of a closed polygon, keeping deviation within `tolerance` pixels.

members.name: Triangulate
members.signature: public static bool Triangulate(Float2[] poly, List<int> outIndices)

docs.summary: Ear-clipping triangulation of a simple polygon. Appends triangle indices (into `poly`) to `outIndices` and returns false if the polygon is degenerate. Holes aren't handled; a hole loop just triangulates as a solid, which is harmless since its texels are transparent.
